decisions: Use a readable dark-fantasy HUD with aged-gold accents around a 16:9 canvas world.
Keep the game dependency-free and draw the tiled environment and original chibi pixel characters entirely in Canvas.
Use crisp handheld-era pixel geometry, four-direction character silhouettes, and square UI framing without copying third-party game assets.
Keep core actions keyboard-first and provide equivalent touch controls on small screens.
Use a compact inventory dialog with equipped slots, a dense item grid, and a persistent comparison/detail pane; collapse it to one scrollable column on phones.
Represent rarity with restrained item borders and labels while keeping procedural Canvas icons and worn layers consistent with the existing pixel geometry.
Use a two-pane forge dialog with a resource ledger and selectable equipment list beside a Canvas workbench; collapse it to a single scrollable column on narrow screens.
Present warrior skills as compact progression cards beside a persistent sword-mastery panel, with a three-slot Canvas hotbar separated from movement and interaction controls.
Present world travel as compact dark-fantasy region cards that clearly separate playable, locked, and planned destinations while preserving the Canvas game as the visual focus.

Reserve separate HUD safe zones for hero status, location, enemy status, objectives, interaction prompts, and the skill hotbar; expose floor advancement as a compact objective action without pausing continuous farm.
Keep cave progression inside the existing objective card: two compact actions for Advance/Stay, one full-width Exit action after a boss, and no blocking completion modal.
